counterevidence_considered.description: The task does not guarantee that each identifier appears exactly once, so uniqueness had to be verified from the staged data; in principle distinct codes could alias one underlying item, but nothing in the visible files supports that, so it cannot demonstrate the issue.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: no uniqueness guarantee stated in task

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. The table stores two disjoint collections of source items. `k1` identifies a first-collection source item measured by column `a`; `k2` identifies a second-collection source item measured by column `b`. The two collections are disjoint. `tag` is an opaque annotation. The row pairing is a storage convention only; there is no matching, pairing, block, or other relationship between the `k1` item and the `k2` item in that row.

evidence.description: All 12 rows carry pairwise-distinct k1 codes (u01–u12) and pairwise-distinct k2 codes, so each identified source item contributes exactly one measurement to the procedure.
evidence.observed_value: 12 distinct k1 and 12 distinct k2 codes over 12 rows (lines 2–13)

evidence.description: The Mann-Whitney U test received one value per unit per side; the statistic 60.5 lies in the valid range for 12 versus 12 entries (max 144), consistent with exactly one entry per row.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify the no-issue verdict by scanning every k1 value (u01–u12) and every k2 value (v07,v09,v11,v13,v15,v17,v19,v21,v23,v01,v03,v05) for duplicates: none exist. I also confirmed the workflow enters each row exactly once and that the reported U statistic is consistent with 12 entries per side. No route to demonstrating repeated unit entry succeeded.
